**Write it as.** `that Amazon S3 path and all folders under that path are registered` · `buckets or prefixes under a bucket, but not individual Amazon S3 objects`

**Scope.** AWS Lake Formation.

> "When you register a location, that Amazon S3 path and all folders under that path are registered."
> — [Adding an Amazon S3 location to your data lake](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/register-data-lake.html)

> "Amazon S3 locations are buckets or prefixes under a bucket, but not individual Amazon S3 objects."
> — [Underlying data access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/access-control-underlying-data.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-registration-requires-iam-role-assumed-for-credentials

**Claim.** You must specify an IAM role when you register an S3 location. Lake Formation assumes that role when it grants temporary credentials to integrated AWS services that access the data in that location.

**Write it as.** `AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role` · `assumes that role when it grants temporary credentials`

**Scope.** AWS Lake Formation.

> "You must specify an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role when you register an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) location. Lake Formation assumes that role when it grants temporary credentials to integrated AWS services that access the data in that location."
> — [Registering an Amazon S3 location](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/register-location.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-registration-role-trust-and-passrole

**Claim.** If you create a registration role using a different path, ensure that the role has a trust relationship with lakeformation.amazonaws.com; the data lake administrator who registers the location must have the iam:PassRole permission on the role.

**Write it as.** `trust relationship with lakeformation.amazonaws.com` · `must have the iam:PassRole permission on the role`

**Scope.** user-defined roles used to register Lake Formation locations.

> "If you create the role using a different path, ensure that the role has a trust relationship with lakeformation.amazonaws.com."
> — [Requirements for roles used to register locations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/registration-role.html)

> "The data lake administrator who registers the location must have the iam:PassRole permission on the role."
> — [Requirements for roles used to register locations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/registration-role.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-remove-iamallowedprincipal-to-enforce-granular-permissions

**Claim.** To provide more granular permissions on a database or table, remove the IAMAllowedPrincipal permission so that Lake Formation enforces the other policies on it. Until it is revoked, a user keeps all the access that IAMAllowedPrincipal gives.

**Write it as.** `remove IAMAllowedPrincipal permission` · `enforces all other policies`

**Scope.** AWS Lake Formation.

> "If you want to provide more granular permissions on a database or table, remove IAMAllowedPrincipal permission and, Lake Formation enforces all other policies associated with that database or table."
> — [Metadata permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/metadata-permissions.html)

> "For example, if there is a policy that allows User A to access Database A with DESCRIBE permissions, and the IAMAllowedPrincipal exists with all permissions, User A will continue to perform all other actions, until the IAMAllowedPrincipal permission is revoked."
> — [Metadata permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/metadata-permissions.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-row-filter-array-map-types-not-supported

**Claim.** The array and map data types are not supported in row filter expressions, but the struct data type is supported.

**Write it as.** `data types aren't supported in row filter expressions` · `The struct data type is supported`

**Scope.** row filter expressions.

> "The array, and map data types aren't supported in row filter expressions. The struct data type is supported."
> — [Data filtering limitations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/data-filtering-notes.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-row-level-security-by-column-values

**Claim.** Granting permissions on a Data Catalog table with row-level security (row filtering) allows users to view only specific rows of data that they have access to in the table, and the filtering is based on the values of one or more columns.

**Write it as.** `view only specific rows of data` · `values of one or more columns`

**Scope.** Lake Formation data filters.

> "Granting permissions on a Data Catalog table with row-level security (row filtering) allows users to view only specific rows of data that they have access to in the table. The filtering is based on the values of one or more columns."
> — [Data filtering and cell-level security in Lake Formation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/data-filtering.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-service-linked-role-default-edit-only-with-custom-role

**Claim.** When registering a location, the default IAM role is the AWSServiceRoleForLakeFormationDataAccess service-linked role, or you can choose a custom role. You can update a registered location only if it was registered with a custom role; otherwise you deregister and register it again.

**Write it as.** `AWSServiceRoleForLakeFormationDataAccess service-linked role (the default)` · `using a custom IAM role`

**Scope.** registered Lake Formation locations; default; not adjustable; service-linked role locations cannot be edited.

> "For IAM role, choose either the AWSServiceRoleForLakeFormationDataAccess service-linked role (the default) or a custom IAM role that meets the requirements in Requirements for roles used to register locations."
> — [Registering an Amazon S3 location](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/register-location.html)

> "You can update a registered location or other details only when you register it using a custom IAM role. To edit a location registered using a service-linked role, you should deregister the location and register it again."
> — [Registering an Amazon S3 location](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/register-location.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-share-across-accounts-orgs-principals

**Claim.** Lake Formation lets you share data internally and externally across multiple AWS accounts, AWS organizations, or directly with IAM principals in another account, with fine-grained access to Data Catalog metadata and underlying data.

**Write it as.** `across multiple AWS accounts, AWS organizations` · `fine-grained access to the Data Catalog metadata`

**Scope.** AWS Lake Formation.

> "Lake Formation also allows you to share data internally and externally across multiple AWS accounts, AWS organizations or directly with IAM principals in another account providing fine-grained access to the Data Catalog metadata and underlying data."
> — [What is AWS Lake Formation?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/what-is-lake-formation.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-storage-enforcement-off-by-default-register-location-and-role

**Claim.** By default, storage-level enforcement is not enabled for Data Catalog tables. To enable it you must register the S3 location of the source data with Lake Formation and provide an IAM role, and it then applies to all tables with the same location path or prefix.

**Write it as.** `storage-level enforcement is not enabled` · `register the Amazon S3 location of your source data with Lake Formation and provide an IAM role`

**Scope.** Data Catalog tables; default; adjustable; S3 location registered with an IAM role.

> "By default, storage-level enforcement is not enabled for tables within the Data Catalog. To enable storage-level enforcement, you must register the Amazon S3 location of your source data with Lake Formation and provide an IAM role. Storage-level permissions will be enabled for all tables with the same table location path or prefix of the Amazon S3 location."
> — [Storage access management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/storage-permissions.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-structured-data-fit-unstructured-use-s3-access-grants

**Claim.** Lake Formation permissions are recommended for structured data arranged in tables with rows and columns. For object-based unstructured data, consider Amazon S3 Access Grants to manage data access.

**Scope.** AWS Lake Formation.

> "Lake Formation permissions are recommended for structured data (arranged in tables with rows and columns). If your data contains object-based unstructured data, consider using Amazon S3 access grants to manage data access."
> — [Adding an Amazon S3 location to your data lake](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/register-data-lake.html)

### lake-formation-two-grant-methods-named-resource-and-lf-tbac

**Claim.** You can grant Lake Formation permissions with the named resource method (choose database and table names) or LF-Tag based access control (LF-TBAC). LF-TBAC groups resources by LF-Tags and is the best way to scale permissions across a huge number of Data Catalog resources.

**Write it as.** `choose database and table names` · `the best way to scale permissions`

**Scope.** AWS Lake Formation.

> "Named resource method – Allows you to choose database and table names while granting permissions to users."
> — [Metadata permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/metadata-permissions.html)

> "LF-TBAC is a feature that allows users to group resources into user-defined categories of LF-Tags and apply permissions on those resource groups. Hence, it is the best way to scale permissions across huge number of Data Catalog resources."
> — [Metadata permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/metadata-permissions.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.

### lake-formation-two-permission-levels-metadata-and-storage

**Claim.** Lake Formation permissions work at two levels: metadata-level permissions on Data Catalog resources such as databases and tables, and storage access permissions on the underlying data in Amazon S3, granted to integrated engines.

> "Managing storage access permissions on the underlying data stored in Amazon S3 on behalf of integrated engines"
> — [AWS Lake Formation: How it works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/how-it-works.html)

> "In Lake Formation, you can implement permissions on two levels:"
> — [AWS Lake Formation: How it works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/how-it-works.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-23.

### lake-formation-unregistered-table-goes-straight-to-s3-bucket-policy

**Claim.** If a table is not managed by Lake Formation, the engine calls S3 directly and the S3 bucket policy and IAM user policy are evaluated for data access.

### lake-formation-vs-iam-who-controls-what

**Claim.** Lake Formation permissions control access to Data Catalog resources, S3 locations and the underlying data, while IAM permissions control access to the Lake Formation and AWS Glue APIs and resources. A Lake Formation CREATE_TABLE permission still fails without the IAM permission on glue:CreateTable.

**Write it as.** `Lake Formation permissions control access to Data Catalog resources, Amazon S3 locations` · `IAM permissions control access`

**Scope.** AWS Lake Formation.

> "Lake Formation permissions control access to Data Catalog resources, Amazon S3 locations, and the underlying data at those locations. IAM permissions control access to the Lake Formation and AWS Glue APIs and resources. So although you might have the Lake Formation permission to create a metadata table in the Data Catalog (CREATE_TABLE), your operation fails if you don't have the IAM permission on the glue:CreateTable API."
> — [Overview of Lake Formation permissions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/lf-permissions-overview.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-15.
